speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. When did you first notice the yellowing of the baby's skin and eyes, and has it spread to the abdomen or legs?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the baby feeding well, and are you noticing an increase in the frequency of wet diapers and stools? Also, has the yellowing progressed to the lower extremities, or is it mostly confined to the face and upper body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of a sibling dying after liver surgery, I am concerned about a metabolic or genetic condition rather than simple breast milk jaundice. I need to assess the baby's overall health and stool characteristics to differentiate between causes like biliary atresia or Galactosemia. REQUEST TEST: Total_and_Direct_Bilirubin, Liver_Function_Tests

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin_Total: 16.1 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.7 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase: 22 U/L, AST: 12 U/L, ALT: 12 U/L

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Born at 39 weeks' gestation. Exclusive breastfeeding. Family history notable for older brother's death possibly related to liver issues. Social history: Not applicable for age.

speaker: Patient
text: Temperature of 37.1°C, pulse of 145/min, and respirations of 40/min. No other symptoms reported by the caregiver. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The family history of a sibling dying after liver surgery is highly suggestive of Galactosemia, a metabolic disorder caused by an inability to process galactose from breast milk. I need to confirm this by checking for reducing substances in the urine, which would indicate galactosemia. REQUEST TEST: Urine_reducing_substances, Blood_glucose, Serum_galactose

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urine_reducing_substances: Positive, Blood_glucose: 65 mg/dL, Serum_galactose: 45 mg/dL

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive urine reducing substances and elevated serum galactose confirm the diagnosis of Galactosemia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Galactosemia
